Validation, error strings, and VM setup for sBPF execution.

# Purpose
This file implements core `fd_vm` support for a Firedancer SBPF virtual machine. It provides error-to-string helpers for VM, eBPF, and syscall failures, so higher layers can write clear log messages for program failure and runtime errors. The file also contains `fd_vm_validate()`, which checks SBPF bytecode against opcode rules, function boundaries, jump targets, syscall and call targets, register limits, and version-dependent instruction support. The validation logic uses a 256-entry opcode map and then applies extra checks for instructions such as `LDDW`, endianness conversion, division, shifts, calls, and static syscalls.

The file also defines the VM object life-cycle and setup functions. `fd_vm_new()`, `fd_vm_join()`, `fd_vm_leave()`, and `fd_vm_delete()` manage VM state in shared memory and check alignment and magic values. `fd_vm_init()` stores execution inputs such as text, rodata, memory regions, syscalls, tracing, and version flags, then prepares the VM for execution. `fd_vm_setup_state_for_execution()` initializes memory configuration, registers, program counter, compute units, and stack state before execution starts. The file also exposes `fd_vm_align()` and `fd_vm_footprint()` so callers can allocate the correct shared-memory size and alignment for the VM object.
